messages.author: 167515a813ea4b70
messages.subject: invariance measurement with many groups
parts:
Hi everyone ,
In my project I want to compare how the level of XY reaction  impacts on the total score of a psychometric instrument (PT score) when  controlled for some other group characteristics . These characteristics are, for example,  gender (2 subgroups), age (5 subgroups), and type of trauma (7 subgroups). The main analysis of the paper is a multiple regression analysis in which level of XY reaction was the predictor variable and the PT score was the outcome. The other characteristics, gender, age  and type of trauma, were included in the multiple regression model as potential confounders variables. A reviewer raised that first I should test for measurement invariance of the psychometric instrument in each group. The problem is that my total sample is n=980 and some groups have a small sample size for CFA analysis. For example, type of trauma is divided into 7 sub-groups ( sample size ranging from 50  to 250 per group). For other groups I have only 2 subgroups and sample size per group ranges from 200 to 680. 
My questions are: considering the type of trauma example, with 7 groups and a small sample size for some groups, is it reasonable to collapse groups with similar types of tramas to increase sample size per group before running multiple group CFA for testing measurement invariance?  If measurement invariance is supported for the collapsed groups, should I rerun the multiple regression analysis but now with the variable type of trauma considering the collapsed groups? Are there any other options or should I remove this variable type of trauma from the main analysis of the paper as I do not have sufficient  sample size to test for measurement invariance across each subgroup? The same question holds for age as I originally divided the sample in 5 sub-groups .
Any suggestions are highly appreciated.


Mirtes G Pereira

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: invariance measurement with many groups
parts:
I would not worry too much about the different sample sizes. You can
still test for measurement invariance. Note that if the main interest is
in regression coefficients, you only need weak invariance (ie equal
factor loadings). There is no need to test for strong invariance (ie
equal intercepts+loadings).

Yves.
